memory_candidates.content: When converting a bare shared-directory git pathspec to an explicit stage_paths[]/similar accumulator list (the 'explicit-pathspec migration' pattern), audit every call site that performs a directory mv/rename specifically: a directory token incidentally covers BOTH the old and new path of a rename, but an explicit list only covers what it names. The migration silently narrows coverage at every rename site unless each one is taught to push both the old and new path together. Neither the directory-pathspec lint (checks for tokens that are too WIDE) nor git-commit-scoped.sh's V2/V5/V6 gates (which only inspect pathspecs they are given) can catch the resulting too-NARROW omission -- it is invisible to both layers by construction.

Before accepting a background run-all.sh/verify-deploy.sh test failure as 'caused by my change', attribute it concretely: (1) check git status/diff on the failing file(s) for pre-existing uncommitted WIP unrelated to your own edits, and if found, git stash push just that file and rerun to see if the failure count is identical with your change absent; (2) check whether the failing suite's file-scope even overlaps your task's touched files at all (different extension entirely is a strong signal of non-attribution). Record the attribution evidence in the plan rather than assuming innocence or guilt.

A newly added scripts/tests/test-*.sh file in a core-extension source store must also be declared in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts list, or the doc-lint deploy gate (check-extension-docs.sh) fails with 'script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts', even though run-all.sh's own glob-based discovery finds and runs the file fine. The two mechanisms (test discovery vs. manifest declaration) are independent; passing the former does not imply passing the latter.
